stories.title: Road to longevity: 7 simple habits that may help ‘super-agers’ stay healthy beyond 100
stories.description: It’s nothing short of a miracle to make it past 100, thriving and with health on your side. After all, being a centenarian is no small feat. But what really goes behind the kind of living that unlocks such a reservoir of health in the “super-agers”? What really blows people away are those rare folks who hit triple digits and still zip around, mentally sharp and mostly free of big illnesses. Scientists have wondered for ages if these people have some hidden biological edge that helps them resist aging.Now, Japanese researchers may have found a clue: in the ultra-elderly, immune systems aren’t just slowing down; they might adapt and get better at fighting threats. A study from Osaka University, published in Cell Reports, found that people over 110 have a higher proportion of rare immune cells (CD4 cytotoxic T lymphocytes). These cells can kill infected and abnormal cells, plus help clear aging and cancerous cells before they cause real trouble. Biology and genetics play a part, but longevity research keeps coming back to simpler stuff: what we eat, how much we move, our sleep habits, and how connected we are with others.

stories.title: DR Congo Gets 70,000 Ebola Vaccines as Outbreak Death Toll Rises
stories.description:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo is set to receive 70,000 doses of the Ervebo Ebola vaccine from the UN-backed International Coordinating Group (ICG). 20,000 doses are reserved for a clinical trial and 50,000 for frontline health workers.
The allocation comes as the country battles its deadliest Ebola outbreak on record. 5,021 cases and 2,325 deaths have been reported so far. However, WHO cautions that it remains unknown whether Ervebo protects against the Bundibugyo strain driving the current outbreak. Early laboratory and animal data suggest it may offer some protection.
The response is further complicated by conflict in eastern DR Congo, which has restricted access to affected communities and hampered contact tracing and safe burials. More than 160 health workers have contracted Ebola, and 40 have died.
